newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST - Spanish stocks helped by EMU, lower rates.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Spanish stocks helped by EMU, lower rates.

text.p: Spanish stocks in 1997 should benefit from government efforts to be part of the first wave of EMU and expectations of monetary easing, according to a Reuters survey of equity forecasts published on Wednesday.

The survey, carried out last week, showed the IBEX 35 climbing to around 5,940 by the end of 1997, an increase of 7.6 percent from the 5,537.55 close on March 12. Eight analysts gave forecasts for 1997.
Predictions for Spanish stocks at the end of 1998 ranged from 6,010 to 7,800.
Spain is hoping to be part of European economic and monetary union from its planned launch on January 1, 1999.
Analysts were more bullish than they were in the last Reuters bourse index poll three months ago when they forecast the IBEX 35 to end 1997 at around 5,490.
PHILLIPE SARDET, HEAD OF EQUITY SALES, CREDIT LYONNAIS SECURITIES ESPANA:

"Performance in 1998 should be tempered by the fact that all the good news on EMU will be factored in (by end 1997). The market will be dominated by stock-picking, and we shouldn't see any strong outperformances in key bluechips such as Telefonica, Endesa or BBV."

"Due to tension over European monetary union, we will see moments of volatility, but we think the market's upside potential is there on the back of the Bank of Spain's capacity to cut interest rates. We'll also be helped by an expected recovery in Germany in the second half."
